captions.threads:
I've cancelled enough subscriptions to know the feeling: that moment when you realize the tool you thought would change everything is just another tab you're not opening anymore.

1/4 The thing about AI tools is they promise transformation but arrive as obligations. You sign up with hope, get hit with a billing cycle before you've even built momentum, and suddenly you're paying for potential instead of results. I learned this the hard way with AI Advantage. The refund window isn't generous, the terms shift depending on which offer you grabbed, and there's always fine print you missed at 11pm when you were tired and excited.

2/4 Before you hit cancel, you need to actually understand what you bought. Different entry points come with different guarantees. Some have 30-day windows. Some don't. The support page won't make this obvious because companies rarely do. You have to read the original confirmation email, check your account settings, and maybe send a support ticket. It's friction by design, not accident.

3/4 The refund terms exist, but they're conditional. Timing matters. How much you've used the tool matters. Whether you're asking through the right channel matters. I've gotten full refunds and I've gotten nothing, depending on when I asked and how I framed it.
